summary:
Project Summary

TerraTrace is an interactive web-based platform designed to identify and analyze environmental changes on Earth using NASA Earth science data.

The platform focuses on important environmental variables such as temperature, rainfall and soil moisture. It collects historical data from NASA sources and displays the changes through interactive graphs, charts and maps.

Users can select a location, choose an environmental variable and compare its changes over different years. The system analyzes the collected data to identify increasing or decreasing trends and estimates the rate of change.

It also uses statistical methods to determine whether the observed trends are significant.

The main aim of TerraTrace is to make complex Earth science data easier to understand and help students, researchers and the public understand how our planet is changing.
details: Project Details Problem Statement Earth's environmental conditions are continuously changing. However, understanding these changes using large amounts of scientific data is difficult. People need a simple tool to identify environmental trends, compare different locations and understand the importance of these changes. Proposed Solution TerraTrace provides an interactive platform that analyzes NASA Earth science data and presents the results in simple visual formats. Main Objectives 1. To identify environmental changes over time. 2. To analyze temperature and rainfall patterns. 3. To compare environmental trends between different locations. 4. To visualize historical data using graphs and maps. 5. To calculate the rate of environmental change. 6. To identify statistically significant trends. 7. To make NASA Earth science data accessible to everyone. Study Area Kerala, India. Proposed locations: - Kochi - Thiruvananthapuram - Wayanad Environmental Variables - Temperature - Rainfall - Soil moisture Technologies Used - Python - Streamlit - Pandas - NumPy - Plotly - SciPy - NASA POWER API Expected Outcome The platform will provide an easy way to understand environmental trends, compare locations and identify important changes using NASA data.
